A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SurfaceBench. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite the revised title, category names and appendix organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original comparisons of symbolic regression methods, including parametric recovery, noise sensitivity, extrapolation, domain-prior ablations and failure analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical evaluations and adds quantitative comparisons of equation similarity with existing benchmarks in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and core discovery/evaluation procedures are retained. Appendix A.4 newly explains implicit-field regression and parametric coordinate fitting, without establishing that the underlying procedures changed.

E1.justification: Appendix A.2 explicitly includes LLM-SRBench in the equation-overlap evaluation, extending the reference corpora beyond AI-Feynman and SRBench named in v1's novelty check. The reported 183-task discovery workload remains unchanged; renamed categories and the completed equation listing do not establish new evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The same four LLM-based and seven non-LLM methods participate in the main comparison. Parametric evaluation still compares OpenEvolve and PySR, and the domain-prior comparison retains the same four methods.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 introduces an overlap-evaluation protocol using operator-set and AST-signature similarities, maximum matches per equation and benchmark-level averages. The implementation text changes Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct to Qwen3-8B, already named in v1's results; this is a reported setting correction, not evidence of rerunning experiments. Sample counts and search budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new memorization-resistance audit quantitatively examines overlap with three prior benchmarks. The existing noise, extrapolation, domain-prior and failure analyses retain their evidence; expanded discussion and disclosed prompts do not constitute additional ablation experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance testing relative to the other. The new similarity averages summarize results rather than introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises OpenEvolve's parametric results: GPT4o-mini NMSE changes from 0.71 to 0.84, Chamfer from 1.85 to 1.22 and Hausdorff from 4.96 to 3.98. Llama and Qwen entries also change, while symbolic accuracies and PySR remain unchanged. New Table 4 reports overlap scores; Tables 1 and 3 and Figures 4–6 retain their results.

T1.justification: The Chamfer, Hausdorff and NMSE formulas and symbolic-equivalence criterion remain unchanged. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs; the added overlap audit supplies procedural descriptions rather than new formal mathematical results.

C1.justification: v2 narrows the scientific-grounding claim to analytically constructed, science-inspired surfaces organized by structural categories. It also removes the claimed fine-tuning analysis from the contributions. The central geometry-aware benchmark contribution and low-recovery claims remain.

C2.justification: The previously largely protocol-focused noise and extrapolation sections gain substantive interpretations about method sensitivity, localized geometric failures and unstable extrapolative growth. v2 also explicitly limits the benchmark to constructed analytic surfaces rather than full governing physical laws. These additions materially expand the paper's explanations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendices A.4–A.5 disclose implicit regression targets, zero-level extraction, independent PySR coordinate fitting, and detailed prior prompts with structured inputs. Table 7 supplies the previously omitted tenth nonlinear-category equation, NCS10. The repository destination and backbone description are also updated, substantially expanding reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Reddy and Shojaee (2025) and removes La Cava et al. (2019). Its comparison with LLM-SRBench shifts from weak scientific grounding toward scalar coverage and missing geometric evaluation, while retaining the same principal research context.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion and substantial explanatory passages are rewritten. Categories and equation identifiers are systematically renamed, section titles are refined, and the inconsistently organized appendix becomes a coherent A.1–A.7 structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is relabeled, an overlap table and two prompt figures are added, and captions, table emphasis and equation-column widths are revised. The empirical plots remain unchanged. Equation-table reformatting also replaces several clear fractions with slash expressions lacking necessary grouping.

improvement.justification: v2 improves task documentation, supplies novelty evidence and better qualifies scientific applicability. However, its equation-table reformatting loses denominator grouping, and its new claim of substantially greater LLM noise degradation is not supported by the unchanged Figure 4. These harms to reproducibility and interpretation offset meaningful gains in transparency, leaving the overall quality direction uncertain.
